best_for: Teams and solo planners who keep docs, wikis and project databases in one shared workspace on Windows or Mac, and who are online most of the day.

points.title: Priced per seat
points.text: Free costs nothing. Plus is listed at USD 10 per seat a month and Business at USD 20; Enterprise is quoted on request. The pricing page says paying yearly saves up to 20 percent. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Where Free stops
points.text: Free keeps 7 days of page history, caps uploads at 5 MB per file and allows 10 guests. Teams on Free get a limited number of blocks; once used up, you can still read and edit but not add new ones. Paid plans raise uploads to 5 GB per file.

points.title: AI is a Business feature
points.text: Notion Agent, AI meeting notes and Enterprise Search (beta) come with Business. Free and Plus only get a limited trial of Notion AI.

points.title: Offline works page by page
points.text: In the desktop and mobile apps you mark each page as available offline, on each device. Business and Enterprise download recent and favorite pages for you. Embeds, forms and buttons need a connection, only the first 50 rows of a database download on their own, and sub-pages must be marked one by one.

points.title: No Linux app
points.text: Notion's help says there is no Linux app and suggests using a browser instead. On Windows there is a per-user installer and an MSIX package (Windows 10 version 2004 or later), both for x64 and Arm64. The Mac app needs macOS 13 or later, with Intel and Apple silicon builds.

points.title: What the desktop app adds
points.text: Command Search opens from the Mac menu bar or Windows taskbar without opening the app, tabs share one running copy to save memory, and you get push notifications for mentions and reminders.

points.title: Long Windows history
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 160 versions. macOS lists only the current release, so an older Mac build needs another source.
